title: WPSS/1744/2026 of DEVENDRA SINGH RANA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Single No. 1744 of 2026
08 July, 2026
Devendra Singh Rana
--Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand & others
--Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Bhupendra Singh Bora, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. K.N. Joshi, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State.
Mr. Rajendra Arya, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. Neeraj
Garg, learned counsel for respondent no.3-UPNL.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Petitioner was engaged as a Driver through
UPNL with respondent no.2 in the year 2018. The
services of the petitioner were disengaged as a Driver
from the respondent-Police Department on the serious
allegation of misbehaving with Km. Bhavna Rawat and
her family members on 22.07.2023 at night after
consuming liquor, vide order dated 27.07.2023, which is
reflected in the order terminating the services of the
petitioner.
2. Petitioner has now moved this Court by filing
the present writ petition for the following prayers:-
"(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the impugned order dated 27.07.2023 passed by
respondent no.2 (S.S.P. Almora) whereby the services of the
petitioner have been terminated, being arbitrary, illegal, voilative of
the principles of natural justice and unsustainable in the eyes of
law. (Annexure No.1 page no.14 to this writ petition).
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to reinstate the petitioner in service
forthwith, with all consequential benefits as may be found
admissible in law.
(iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus

2
commanding the respondents to consider and decide the
representation of the petitioner dated 03.07.2026 in accordance
with law, within a stipulated period as may be fixed by this
Hon'ble Court. (Annexure Nos.5 & 6 page no.21-24) to this writ
petition."
3. Since allegations contained in the order dated
27.07.2023 have not been inquired into by the
respondent-department and, straightway, petitioner was
disengaged, appears to be in violation of the principles of
natural justice.
4. In such view of the matter, interference only to
this extent is made that petitioner may file a
representation to respondent no.2 within a period of two
weeks from today requesting him to forward the name of
the petitioner to respondent no.3-UPNL for
re-engagement of the petitioner as a Driver with the
Police Department. If such representation is moved by
the petitioner within two weeks, as stated above, the said
representation shall be decided by respondent no.2
sympathetically by a reasoned and speaking order,
keeping in view that the allegations levelled against the
petitioner were not inquired into and the principles of
natural justice were not followed while disengaging the
petitioner in the earlier occasion, within a period of eight
weeks from the date of receipt of such representation
filed by the petitioner.
5. The writ petition is accordingly disposed of
finally.
6. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of
accordingly.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
